scene: A clear home play mat with Bear Peer sitting screen left and Child sitting screen right, angled toward each other and close enough for a short hand-to-hand pass. Peer is the same small brown bear, age four, in his teal T-shirt; Child is the four-year-old tiger boy in his yellow T-shirt. Exactly one small red ball is present. Peer can roll it about twenty centimeters between his own hands in front of his knees; a separate clear short path between the friends will allow Child's later roll back. No truck, blocks, targets, extra balls or other props. Locked 16:9 medium two-shot keeps both faces, knees, hands and the full ball path visible.

emotion.baseline: Calm, warm and regulated baseline. Both friends speak at ordinary play volume and keep relaxed seated postures.
emotion.allowed_shift: Peer shows a small earnest look when requesting one final roll. Child considers and confirms the order, watches attentively and shows a small appreciative smile after receiving the ball; neither needs to look delighted about waiting.
emotion.forbidden: No grabbing, sulking used to force agreement, pressured smiling, shouting, jumping frenzy, competitive cheering, frantic gestures or elastic faces. The ball moves slowly and stays on the mat during each roll.

clips.start: Peer steadies the one red ball under his right palm in front of his knees, with his left hand twenty centimeters away. Child sits close on the right with his hands resting on his own knees.
clips.action: Peer gently rolls the ball from his right palm into his waiting left hand during the opening turn, making his current play visible. The ball has stopped before Child requests the next turn. Peer holds it still as he asks for one additional roll; Child confirms the order and settles in to watch how Peer rolls it, leaving control with Peer. This opening roll precedes the agreement and is distinct from the single final roll in the next clip.
clips.end: The red ball is stopped beneath Peer's left palm in front of his knees. His right hand rests twenty centimeters away, and Child watches attentively with his hands on his own knees.

clips.start: The red ball is stopped beneath Peer's left palm in front of his knees. His right hand rests twenty centimeters away, and Child watches attentively with his hands on his own knees.
clips.action: Peer rolls the ball once from his left hand into his waiting right palm — exactly the single agreed final roll — and stops it fully. Only then does he lift the ball a few centimeters and place it directly into Child's open hands; this transfer is not another solo roll. Child receives it before thanking him and announcing his plan to roll it back.
clips.end: Child holds the single red ball in both hands after the completed handoff. Peer sits with open hands ready nearby; no further roll has happened yet.

clips.start: Child holds the single red ball in both hands after the completed handoff. Peer sits with open hands ready nearby; no further roll has happened yet.
clips.action: Peer offers his open paws as the catching target during his line. Child sets the same ball on the clear mat and gives it a short, slow roll toward Peer on his playful send-off line. Peer catches it gently with both paws and stops it on the mat. The visible sequence is finished Peer turn, handoff, thanks, then Child's first roll; both remain seated throughout.
clips.end: Peer cups the same red ball on the mat after catching Child's first roll. Child's hands are relaxed in front of him and both friends remain seated with small smiles, ready to continue the shared rolling game.
